title: Jerome by John J Caswell Jr at Playwrights Horizons #playwrightshoriz...
transcript: Not to yuck anyone's yum, but when a gay couple brings in a third, how frequently does it work out? It's probably an uphill battle if the threesome originated out of some issue with the two person dynamic, but Jerome by John Caswell Jr is more concerned with exploring how this type of arrangement evolves rather than harping on how or why it was initiated. Set in Arizona in the early 90s, Cornelius and Doane come across Bruin who recently fled San Francisco for reasons not immediately clear. Thing between the three of them start off with a bang (wink, wink) but over time, a cold mortality looms over their relationship, evoking questions around responsibility, care, and self-preservation. The triangular lens becomes really interesting here when you consider a world where only two of them remain, but not the original two. I was fascinated by the dynamic this play presented, and while it had its clunky moments, it offered just as many funny or tender ones, too. This was also a rare case where I wouldn't have minded a little more exposition. I felt like some areas of the story deserved more attention than they were given, or vice versa. I'm glad it has more time to cook before it officially opens, but I enjoyed it regardless. The post-apocalyptic aesthetic, the interesting progression of the story, and the fantastic performance by Tony winner Stephen Spinella was more than enough to make the two and a half hours fly. With that, another program for my collection.
